protocol.origin: Research-agent C1, then protocol designer live-20260928T143347-906294. Engineering amendments below are by the coding assistant, not attributed to autonomous research discovery.
protocol.review: Bound review live-20260928T143721-035518 advised implementation but incorrectly called the hypothesis and graph example consistent. Its approval is not a semantic certificate. The historical outputs remain unchanged.
protocol.research_question: For the same model recovery plan and visible tool receipts, how do full versus declared-dependency replay change correct completion and tool work on source updates, with and without a missing dependency?
protocol.hypothesis: With complete declared lineage, selective and full replay should produce the same current artifact with less work when an unaffected branch exists. With missing lineage, selective replay can leave stale output unless the model plan explicitly repairs the missing path. Full replay may improve correctness at extra work. These mechanisms are prior art; the study tests their interaction with model-proposed recovery plans, not a new attribution algorithm.
engineering_amendments: Correct the hypothesis: a missing critical edge can make selective replay WRONG while full replay is correct, unless the model requests sufficient extra work. Equality is not a failure when the model repairs the omitted path.

Use an actual fork/join graph: read_main -> summarize_main -> combine -> report; read_aux -> summarize_aux -> combine. Remove summarize_aux -> combine in the incomplete-lineage scenario. The original example removed an edge that was not in its stated chain and claimed an impossible closure.

Generate the healthy cached receipts at source v1; apply the source update and declared-edge omission before presenting the observation to the recovery-plan model. Both updated scenarios have exactly the same current source values. No mid-request source changes occur.

Execute tool nodes against explicit cached receipts. A rerun is always a tool call; there is no automatic content-keyed cache refresh or implicit traversal of actual dependencies. Without this rule, the proposed cache key would silently repair the intervention and conflate policies.

A executes model reruns in listed order; B is A plus one transient retry; C unions requested nodes with all nodes after any source change; D unions requested nodes with the changed source and declared transitive dependents. C/D deduplicate and topologically order. All honor model refusal. Work caps include attempts; emit does not consume a tool call and emits the cached report.

There are no transient errors in these three scenarios. B is therefore an explicit error-only negative control and is expected to match A. Its retry behavior is checked in software tests, not represented as an observed scientific advantage.

The source update is legitimate, and the missing edge is a lineage defect. This is an operational refinement of C1, not a benchmark of multiple independently injected tool failures; no broad compound-fault robustness claim is allowed.

The correctness evaluator independently computes the artifact from current source rows. Its implementation and answers are never inputs to the model or policy. The source's classification labels are ordinary task data read through tools, distinct from private final correctness labels.

Replace invalid falsifiers with observable paired outcomes: relative correctness of C/D per scenario, extra work, whether model-requested nodes cover the missing path, and false refusal in clean cases. Do not infer equivalence from a small zero difference or define any number of successes as exceeding an evaluator count.

These are six self-authored base instances with three paired scenarios, not 72 independent samples. Publish all instance results and descriptive paired differences, without significance, power, deployment-rate or external-validity claims. No hidden holdout is claimed.

Freeze source, protocol, prompts, datasets, declared graphs and current inputs before the run. Use 18 single model calls and 72 CPU replays; the shared model cost is counted once per episode, not once per policy. Six prior campaign calls plus 18 exhaust the 24-request research-v2 cap. No automatic retry or new campaign is permitted.

limitations: Six self-authored base instances; scenarios and policies are repeated measures, not independent samples.
One cached model recovery plan per episode, not four independent interactive agents.
Missing terminal emit is malformed output, not voluntary model refusal or a wrong numerical answer.
Post-hoc normalization adds only emit after an existing final rerun(report); no recovery nodes are invented.
Post-hoc equality is not a preregistered success, held-out confirmation or statistical equivalence.
Selective replay did not outperform the model plan alone; do not cherry-pick full replay as the sole baseline.
No transient errors were injected, so retry B is expected to match A.
Existing selective invalidation and version lineage are prior art; novelty is unestablished.

methodological_corrections: A constant-label evaluator necessarily removes any accuracy difference. Its collapse is not evidence of oracle leakage; delete that proposed control.

A deterministic reference is valid for fully specified CPU tasks. Independence requires different implementation from the policy and no reference labels in its inputs, not a claim that all deterministic scoring is tautological.

A static import check or separate Python process does not establish a security sandbox. Describe the actual data-flow boundary and test it by changing private labels while holding public inputs fixed.
Do not infer workflow floor effects from the unrelated earlier huge-integer pilot. Preserve the negative pilot without further model capability calibration.
The ACM full-text limitation copied into the refiner output belongs to an earlier candidate and is not evidence about this arXiv-based proposal.

Specify a concrete difference between local repair, transitive invalidation and the proposed adapter before spending experiment calls. If identical, collapse the conditions and report the lack of a new mechanism.

Define failure persistence, clean and legitimate-update controls, all policies' observation access, tool-work allowance, and exact API call arithmetic. A prose maximum of six calls is not a cost decomposition.
Fixture/fault variants sharing one initial plan are paired repeated measures, not independent model samples. Reject-all is not successful completion.

source_check.scope: Focused version-specific primary-source recheck, not exhaustive search or reproduction

notes.finding: The published scope uses one fault per intervention and excludes compound/cascading evaluation. Its authored data-quality scenarios are hypothesis-generating, and primary deterministic checks remain fallible.

The author distinguishes post-hoc framing from prospective validation and warns that repeated seeds on authored fixtures measure output stability rather than independent task designs. High deterministic lifecycle pass counts are not deployment-rate evidence.

The paper uses simulated tools and single-parameter injection; multi-parameter/multi-turn propagation is outside that version. Limited human labels and evaluator errors constrain interpretation of absolute rates.

design_implications: Do not label numeric reseeding of the existing six instances independent validation.
Distinguish novel task structures, changed data values, repeated model outputs and paired policy replays.
Avoid claiming reproduction of published baselines without their actual implementations.
Method comparisons can be useful as scoped empirical evidence even when the mechanism is prior art.
